why: Next.js declares no routes. The FILE TREE is the route table: `pages/index.tsx` answers `/`, `pages/content/[id].tsx` answers `/content/{id}`, and nothing in the source says so. Every other router pack here reads a declaration; this one reads a convention, which is why it needs a shape of its own (`filesystem`) rather than a `routeObject`. Two conventions ship in one product: the pages router every Next.js application before 13 uses, and the app router after it.
matching: a source file under a `root` directory of a package that depends on `next`, by extension; the route is the file's path under that directory
